prompted_for: Which standard governs which part of the plant (compliance standards as a plant map)
composition: portrait navy sheet with thin border and breadcrumb
centred light uppercase headline and subtitle
plant schematic fills the middle, split into zones (generation, storage, pure steam, controls, fabrication)
labels with standard codes placed in the margins beside each zone
faint dashed construction grid dividing the sheet
loose two-tier repetition of the plant
layout_devices: dotted leader lines from labels to zones
dashed construction grid with crosshair markers
palette: pale steel-blue highlight block and subtle accent label
typography: regular sans standard codes in small lists
motion_implied: leader lines draw from zone to label
t2i_keywords: process train of vessels and membranes
t2i_prompt: Dark navy blueprint sheet with a thin border and a faint dashed construction grid with crosshair markers. A light wide uppercase headline centred at the top. Below, an annotated plant schematic in white hairline strokes, divided into outlined zones; each zone connects by a dotted leader line to a margin label in small uppercase sans with a short list beneath: <CONTENT>. One zone filled with a pale steel-blue block as the active highlight. Flat vector, semi-isometric equipment, no shading, generous navy negative space, precise architectural-plan feel.
signature_idea: Standards stop being a list and become labels pinned onto the part of the plant they govern.
strengths: answers a real QA question (which standard where) at a glance
on-brand navy with one steel-blue accent
maps naturally to an interactive hotspot component
light headline close to Geist light
weaknesses: plant drawn twice and qualification label duplicated
labels small and hard to read
includes stainless welding torches off-offer for PP systems
brand_fit_why: Navy ground, hairline art, single steel-blue highlight and light caps headline are on-brand; duplication and crowding reduce precision.
